title: Projects and folders isolate blast radius per environment
statement: The resource hierarchy (folders/projects) isolates each environment and plane so a failure or policy change in one project cannot reach another; the hierarchy is never a runtime dependency.
rationale: A shared project lets a dev mistake or credential reach production resources.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Each committed tfvars names a distinct project and nothing at runtime calls Resource Manager; reusing one project id across two environments fails the check.

notes: Folder creation is organisation-scoped and outside this repository's Terraform root.

title: Workforce identity comes from Cloud Identity
statement: Human (workforce) access to the platform's GCP resources and admin surfaces authenticates through Cloud Identity accounts, not ad-hoc or shared identities.
rationale: Shared or unmanaged human identities make privileged actions unattributable.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every human principal granted in Terraform/IAP is a managed user/group; a literal shared account or allUsers grant fails.

title: Privileged access is just-in-time through PAM
statement: Privileged (admin/break-glass) access to production projects is granted just-in-time and time-bounded through Privileged Access Manager rather than standing role bindings.
rationale: Standing admin grants are the authority an attacker or a misbehaving agent inherits.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A PAM entitlement exists for each privileged role and no human holds that role as a standing binding; a standing owner/editor binding fails.

notes: Also phase 0 deliverable of §26.

title: Organization Policy enforces non-bypassable guardrails
statement: Organization Policy constraints enforce platform guardrails (e.g. no service-account keys, no external IPs, resource locations) so no project-level actor can bypass them.
rationale: A guardrail held only by convention is undone by the first person in a hurry.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Policies are declared and an acceptance test asserts each; deleting the policy resource fails the test.

title: Cloud Asset Inventory records asset and change history
statement: Cloud Asset Inventory (feeds or exports) records every resource and its changes so drift and unmanaged resources can be found.
rationale: An unmanaged resource is invisible until it costs money or leaks data.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: An asset feed/export resource exists and its sink is readable; removing it fails a plan assertion.

title: Security Command Center reports posture with no hot-path dependency
statement: Security Command Center collects posture findings for every project; nothing in the trading path depends on it.
rationale: Misconfiguration found only by an attacker.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: SCC custom modules are planned in each environment; the edge-node and brains link no SCC client.

title: Cloud Audit Logs capture admin and data-access evidence
statement: Admin-activity and data-access audit logs are enabled for every service holding secrets, keys, ledger, evidence or model data.
rationale: An access nobody logged cannot be investigated.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: An IAM audit config enables DATA_READ/DATA_WRITE for each sensitive service; removing a service from it fails the test.

title: Isolated Reflex, Fabric, Service, Data and Engineering VPCs
statement: Separate VPC networks exist for Reflex, Fabric, Service, Data and Engineering traffic, each deny-by-default on ingress.
rationale: One flat network lets a compromised research workload reach the execution path.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Five google_compute_network resources with deny-ingress rules are planned; merging two into one fails the module tests.

title: Network Connectivity Center hub-spoke with route filters
statement: VPCs and hybrid links connect through an NCC hub/spoke with route filters, and regional trading continues when remote spokes are unavailable.
rationale: Ad-hoc peering creates unintended transitive reachability between isolated networks.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: An NCC hub and spokes with include/exclude ranges are planned; a spoke without filters fails.

title: Cloud Router provides dynamic BGP for Interconnect and VPN
statement: Hybrid links (Interconnect, HA VPN) exchange routes dynamically through Cloud Router BGP sessions.
rationale: Static routes on hybrid links fail silently when a provider path moves.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A router with BGP peers for each attachment/tunnel is planned.

title: Private provider connectivity with HA VPN fallback
statement: Provider, colo, custody and IBM connectivity uses Dedicated/Partner/Cross-Cloud Interconnect where available, with HA VPN or internet fallback only where acceptable.
rationale: Venue and custody traffic over the public internet adds latency and attack surface.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Interconnect attachment and HA VPN gateway are planned together; an attachment without fallback fails the module test.

title: Cloud NAT controls egress for non-latency-critical workloads
statement: Internet egress for scouts, agents and builders goes through Cloud NAT with logging; Reflex venue egress is governed separately from that path.
rationale: Uncontrolled egress is an exfiltration path; coupling venue egress to shared NAT couples trading to crawler load.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every NAT translates only named subnets to reserved addresses and logs; a NAT covering all subnets fails.

title: Agent and crawler web egress is policy-controlled and audited
statement: Agent and crawler web egress passes a policy/audit proxy (Secure Web Proxy where suitable) so every outbound destination is allowed by policy and logged.
rationale: An agent that can fetch any URL can exfiltrate or be steered by any page.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Egress from agent/scout workloads is only possible through the proxy and the proxy allowlist is declared; a direct route fails.

notes: ADR 0024 chose an in-tree Envoy egress sidecar rather than Secure Web Proxy.

title: Private Service Connect for managed APIs, never on the hot path
statement: Managed Google/service endpoints are reached via Private Service Connect where supported, and no PSC hop sits on the trading hot path.
rationale: Public API endpoints widen the exfiltration surface.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A PSC endpoint is planned for Google APIs; none fronts the execution node venue path.

title: Private Google Access on every subnet
statement: Every subnet reaches Google APIs over Private Google Access without public addresses.
rationale: Workloads given external IPs to reach Google APIs become internet-exposed.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every google_compute_subnetwork sets private_ip_google_access=true; one without fails the test.

title: Cloud DNS zones and Fabric bootstrap SRV records
statement: Cloud DNS serves public and private zones, and Fabric clients bootstrap brokers from SRV records; critical internal names use resilient zones and clients tolerate DNS loss with cached/local behaviour.
rationale: Hard-coded broker addresses break on replacement; DNS loss must not stop trading.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A private zone with SRV records per broker is planned and the client resolves them; hard-coded broker addresses fail.

title: Global ALB is the only public ingress for portal and API
statement: Public client traffic reaches portal/BFF/API only via HTTPS Global External ALB fronting Cloud Run (or GKE Gateway).
rationale: Directly exposed services bypass WAF, TLS policy and rate limits.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: The ALB/forwarding rules exist and every Cloud Run service ingress is internal or internal-and-cloud-load-balancing; a public run.app ingress fails.

title: Load balancers never front Reflex or Fabric
statement: No load balancer, gateway or mesh hop fronts Reflex execution nodes or Fabric brokers.
rationale: A balancer on the venue path adds latency and an unplanned failure domain.

verification.check: Scanning Terraform finds no backend/NEG that targets an execution-node or broker group; adding one fails.

title: Cloud Armor WAF/DDoS/rate policy on the public edge
statement: Every internet-facing backend has a Cloud Armor policy with WAF, adaptive DDoS protection and per-client rate limiting; the edge may deny clients without trading impact.
rationale: An unprotected edge is the cheapest denial of service.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every security policy enables layer-7 adaptive protection and a rate-based ban; removing either fails the tests.

title: Cloud CDN accelerates public static content only
statement: Public static assets are served through Cloud CDN with an explicit cache mode; dynamic/API backends are not cached.
rationale: Caching an API response leaks one client's data to another.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every backend bucket enables CDN with explicit cache mode and no backend service does.

title: Certificate Manager issues public TLS certificates
statement: Public TLS certificates for the edge are issued and rotated by Certificate Manager (or managed certificates), never uploaded by hand.
rationale: Hand-managed certificates expire and take the edge down.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Certificate resources are managed; a self-managed certificate block fails.

title: IAP protects every admin interface
statement: Admin interfaces (consoles, Argo CD, Kargo, node shells) are reachable only through Identity-Aware Proxy.
rationale: An admin surface on a public address is the most direct route to production authority.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Remote-admin firewall rules admit only the IAP range and every admin service has an IAP binding; a rule from 0.0.0.0/0 fails.

title: Hierarchical firewall policies segment networks
statement: Network segmentation is enforced by Cloud NGFW / hierarchical firewall policies inherited from the organisation, in addition to per-VPC rules.
rationale: Per-VPC rules can be widened by any project editor.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A hierarchical/network firewall policy is planned and associated; absence fails.

title: Dedicated C4/C4D-class VMs run Reflex and Fabric
statement: Reflex and Fabric run on dedicated Compute Engine C4/C4D-class VMs, pre-provisioned per shard, with a zonal fenced standby.
rationale: Shared or autoscaled compute introduces latency jitter and noisy neighbours on the order path.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: The node module accepts only the C-class allowlist, declares primary and standby templates in different zones; a non-C machine type is refused at plan.

notes: ADR 0024: one Compute Engine node per region.

title: Reflex state is ephemeral and rebuilt after restart
statement: Reflex order books, features, session and model state live in RAM/Local SSD only and are rebuilt from the feed and the deployed package after a restart, never trusted from a previous process.
rationale: A restarted node acting on its previous run's book or resting orders trades on state nobody verified.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A restarted node with a prior session refuses to form orders until venue reconciliation completes and rebuilds books from the feed; removing the reconciliation arm fails.

title: Fabric broker journals on persistent Hyperdisk
statement: Fabric broker journals persist on Hyperdisk/persistent disks; Local SSD is cache only.
rationale: A journal on ephemeral disk loses acknowledged records with the VM.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: The broker template attaches a persistent hyperdisk journal device; a local-SSD journal fails.

title: Fabric journal is RF3 across zones with quorum before durable ack
statement: Fabric durable partitions replicate RF3 across three zones and acknowledge durable only after a quorum persisted; regional quorum with selective async cross-region mirrors.
rationale: A single-disk broker loses acknowledged financial outcomes when the disk or zone fails.

verification.check: A broker cluster test kills one replica after ack and every acknowledged record is still readable; an RF1 configuration fails.

title: Reservations guarantee production hot capacity
statement: Production hot capacity (Reflex, Fabric) is backed by specific Compute Engine reservations sized to target; commitments are used to control cost.
rationale: A zone stock-out at restart leaves a region unable to trade.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every machine group consumes a specific reservation sized to its target; an unreserved group fails.

title: Critical VMs boot as Shielded VMs
statement: Every VM-based critical service boots with Secure Boot, vTPM and integrity monitoring.
rationale: An unattestable boot chain is an unattestable chain of custody.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every instance template enables the three shielded options; removing one fails.

title: Regional GKE Standard hosts warm services, solvers, agents and sinks
statement: Warm domain/control services, solvers, agents and sinks run on regional GKE Standard clusters with a regional control plane and multi-zone node pools.
rationale: Zonal clusters lose the control plane with one zone.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Regional GKE Standard clusters with multi-zone pools are planned per region.

notes: Conflicts with ADR 0024: warm binaries run on Cloud Run, no Kubernetes for workloads. ADR 0036 allows a GitOps control-plane cluster only.

title: Cloud Service Mesh provides mTLS for warm services only
statement: Warm services communicate over mTLS with traffic policy (Cloud Service Mesh), and the mesh never carries Reflex traffic.
rationale: Plaintext service-to-service traffic is readable and forgeable inside the VPC.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Warm-service traffic is mTLS; reflex nodes are outside the mesh.

notes: Service Mesh presumes GKE; conflicts with ADR 0024.

title: Cloud Run only where cold-start and latency fit the SLO
statement: Cloud Run/Cloud Run Jobs host bursty stateless APIs, scouts, webhooks and agent jobs, and are not used where cold-start or latency violates an SLO.
rationale: A cold start on a latency-sensitive service is an SLO breach nobody planned.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every Cloud Run service on a latency-sensitive path holds a warm minimum instance; an SLO-bound service at min 0 fails.

notes: ADR 0024 places every warm binary on Cloud Run, including the brains, which the blueprint would put on GKE.

title: Cloud Storage holds replay lake, segment archive, models and evidence
statement: Cloud Storage holds the tick/internal replay lake, Fabric segment archive, model weights, compact knowledge packs and internal evidence, under lifecycle classes.
rationale: Without a durable archive, replay and audit depend on hot stores that are bounded.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Buckets for archive, artifacts and evidence exist with lifecycle/retention rules; fabricd archives to a GCS blob store.

title: External world payloads are never retained
statement: Raw external-world content is not warehoused: only derived knowledge packs and internal/tick history are retained.
rationale: Retaining raw third-party content creates licensing and privacy liability with no replay value.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A knowledge pack carrying an undeclared field (e.g. a raw body) is refused at decode; removing deny_unknown_fields fails the test.

title: Bigtable holds rebuildable high-rate derived state
statement: Bigtable stores high-rate derived time-series, features and replay indexes, rebuildable from retained sources, with replication only as justified.
rationale: A hot store treated as source of record makes its loss a data loss.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Instance is planned with autoscaling; a rebuild job from GCS/Fabric repopulates it.

title: BigQuery serves research and may lag without trading impact
statement: BigQuery holds research, resolved forecast scores, backtests and analytics; it can lag without trading impact.
rationale: Coupling the warehouse to the trading path makes analytics load a trading risk.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: The research dataset exists and the edge node links no BigQuery client.

title: Knowledge Catalog provides governance, lineage and quality
statement: Knowledge Catalog (Dataplex) records governance, lineage, quality and data products for platform data.
rationale: Data without lineage cannot be trusted for a decision that must be explained.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Catalog entries/lineage exist for the data stores.

title: Dataflow is batch/reprocessing only, never the live bus
statement: Dataflow (and Dataproc Serverless) is used only for large batch/reprocessing and Spanner change-stream pipelines, never as the primary live bus.
rationale: A batch engine on the live path inherits batch latency and failure modes.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: No Dataflow job/resource consumes or produces a live Fabric stream.

title: Memorystore is a non-authoritative cache only
statement: Memorystore/Redis holds only non-authoritative warm cache; its loss causes recompute or cache miss, never financial inconsistency.
rationale: A cache mistaken for a source of record loses positions on failover.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Every composition root refuses Memorystore as a store of record; persistence is disabled; setting a root's store to Redis stops start-up.

title: AlloyDB holds operational relational metadata
statement: Operational relational metadata and workflows live in AlloyDB.
rationale: Metadata scattered across files cannot be queried or backed up consistently.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: AlloyDB cluster/instance planned with a writer.

title: Spanner Enterprise Plus is authoritative financial truth
statement: Ledger, positions, obligations, capital and idempotency records live in Spanner Enterprise Plus with multi-region HA, isolated from analytics workloads.
rationale: Financial truth on a single-node store is lost or split by a regional failure.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A ledger writer commits to a multi-region Enterprise Plus database and no analytics workload reads it directly.

notes: A Spanner client needs gRPC/TLS/Google auth, which ADR 0002/0009 do not admit in-tree.

title: Spanner Graph holds promoted world knowledge apart from the ledger
statement: Promoted world/causal/affordance knowledge lives in Spanner Graph in a database and workload boundary separate from the ledger, so graph query load cannot affect money truth; temporary hypotheses stay ephemeral.
rationale: Noisy analytical graph load on the ledger database degrades financial commits.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A graph database distinct from the ledger database is planned; evidence workers write it.

title: Vertex AI APIs behind Algorik adapters
statement: Training, managed agents, evaluation and model lifecycle use Vertex AI / Agent Platform APIs only through Algorik adapters, so product contracts do not depend on Google branding or API shape.
rationale: Provider churn leaking into contracts forces a product rewrite on every rename.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Only the adapter module names Vertex endpoints; contracts carry Algorik types.

title: Model registry records version, evaluation and lineage
statement: Every model version carries evaluation and lineage in a registry; if the registry is unavailable promotion pauses while existing packages continue.
rationale: A model without lineage cannot be explained or rolled back.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Promotion refuses without a passing evaluation and a stable digest; registry unavailability refuses promotion but leaves served models running.

title: Cloud Build private pools build and test privately
statement: CI builds and tests run on Cloud Build private pools reached from GitHub via WIF; if unavailable, deployment pauses and runtime is unchanged.
rationale: Builds on shared public runners expose source and signing paths to a wider supply chain.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A worker pool exists and deploy.yml submits builds to it; a build on ubuntu-latest fails.

title: Immutable artifacts in Artifact Registry, replicated
statement: Images, packages and OCI release/model manifests are stored immutably in Artifact Registry; critical artifacts are replicated and running nodes keep local copies.
rationale: A mutable or deletable registry lets a released digest disappear or change.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Repositories set immutable tags and no identity can delete; a replica/remote repository exists.

title: Images are vulnerability-scanned before release
statement: Every image is vulnerability-scanned (Artifact Analysis metadata) and a failing scan blocks release.
rationale: A signed vulnerable image is a vulnerability with a certificate.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: deploy.yml scans before push/sign and fails on CRITICAL; removing the step fails the pipeline gate test.

title: Binary Authorization blocks unattested deploys
statement: Deploy-time admission enforces build/signing attestations and blocks unsafe deploys by design.
rationale: Without enforcement any pushed image runs.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Policy requires attestation with ENFORCED_BLOCK_AND_AUDIT_LOG and every Cloud Run service is subject to it; a dry-run policy fails.

title: CI and workloads authenticate keylessly via WIF
statement: GitHub Actions and external CI obtain short-lived credentials through Workload Identity Federation; no service-account key exists anywhere.
rationale: A downloaded key is a credential that outlives every review.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: The pipeline authenticates via the WIF provider, no key resource exists, and org policy disables key creation; adding a key fails.

title: IAM is deny-by-default and least privilege per workload
statement: Every workload has its own identity with only the grants it uses; nothing runs as the default compute identity.
rationale: A shared or broad identity turns one compromise into all.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Each deployable has its own SA, none uses the default compute SA, and every SA runs or signs something.

title: Secrets come from Secret Manager, never Git or environment
statement: Venue, API and service secrets are held in Secret Manager, read by authorized workloads only, mounted as files with bounded startup behaviour; no secret is in Git.
rationale: A secret in Git or the environment leaks to every reader and child process.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: No secret value in Terraform; every secret is mounted as a file and granted per workload; venue credential unreadable where live trading is impossible.

title: KMS provides CMEK and signing; runtime survives key outage
statement: Cloud KMS provides CMEK and release/package/ledger signing keys; key availability is required for new promotions but not for the currently running package.
rationale: A runtime that needs KMS for every action halts trading on a KMS outage.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Keys rotate and data keys cannot be destroyed; the running edge node holds no KMS client on its decision path.

title: Cloud HSM for higher-assurance keys where required
statement: Signing and key material requiring higher assurance uses Cloud HSM protection.
rationale: Software keys are exportable by anyone with enough access to the project.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: kms_protection_level=HSM in environments that require it.

title: Private CA issues mTLS identity for Fabric and VMs
statement: Certificate Authority Service issues private mTLS identities for Fabric brokers, clients and VMs.
rationale: Without mTLS any host on the network can impersonate a broker or producer.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A CA pool exists and Fabric clients/brokers present certificates from it.

notes: In-tree TLS is refused by ADR 0009; mTLS would come from a sidecar.

title: VPC Service Controls perimeter around data, AI and ledger
statement: A VPC Service Controls perimeter encloses data, AI and ledger services to prevent exfiltration.
rationale: Valid credentials alone can copy a dataset out of the project.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A service perimeter covering the data/AI/ledger APIs is planned.

notes: Requires organisation access policy.

title: Sensitive Data Protection discovers and redacts sensitive data
statement: Sensitive Data Protection discovers, classifies and redacts sensitive data in stores and logs.
rationale: Unclassified sensitive data leaks through logs and exports.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Discovery config/inspect templates exist for data stores.

title: Cloud Monitoring and Managed Prometheus collect metrics and alerts
statement: Metrics, SLOs and alerts flow to Cloud Monitoring and Managed Service for Prometheus, with buffering/sampling so observability loss cannot block trading.
rationale: A process nothing can see cannot be operated.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Alert policies exist on series the binaries record and a scrape/ingestion of those series is observed.

title: Cloud Logging receives control and application logs
statement: Control and application logs land in Cloud Logging with bounded volume.
rationale: Logs that are unbounded or missing make incidents unreconstructable.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Workloads log to stdout/stderr on Cloud Run; NAT and flow logs enabled; per-event logging is rate-bounded.

title: Cloud Trace covers warm and API paths
statement: Warm/API requests emit traces to Cloud Trace.
rationale: Latency regressions across services cannot be localised without traces.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: A trace exported per API request is observed.

title: Connectivity Tests verify network reachability
statement: Network Intelligence Center Connectivity Tests verify intended and forbidden paths.
rationale: Firewall intent drifts from reality without a reachability check.

sources.section: §19 Complete GCP Service Catalog for This Platform

verification.check: Connectivity test resources for key paths exist.

title: Every cloud service has a reason, connections, scaling and degraded mode
statement: Every cloud service/workload added has one primary reason, known upstream/downstream connections, a scaling model and a degraded-mode contract, with a documented state owner; services without a distinct capability are not added.
rationale: An unexplained service is cost and attack surface with no owner.

verification.check: Each catalogue entry carries owner, connections, scaling and degraded-mode fields and a test refuses an entry missing one.

title: Fabric mirrors only configured critical topics asynchronously
statement: The Rust Fabric uses regional quorum durability with selective asynchronous cross-region mirrors; mirroring never blocks local commit.
rationale: Synchronous cross-region mirroring couples every region's commit latency to the slowest link.

verification.check: A mirror stalled for a topic does not delay a local produce ack; only declared topics mirror.

title: Managed agents degrade to backlog, never an execution dependency
statement: Managed agent runtime (Vertex Agent Engine where suitable) may hold sessions/memory/A2A; if it fails, agents degrade to backlog and execution is unaffected.
rationale: An agent platform on the execution path makes model availability a trading dependency.

verification.check: Edge node links no agent crate and trades identically when the centre stops answering.

title: Training is queue/quota-aware and uses Spot where interruptible
statement: Custom training/evaluation is queue- and quota-aware and uses Spot/preemptible capacity where interruption is safe.
rationale: On-demand capacity for disposable training is pure overspend.

verification.check: Training job specs mark interruptible jobs Spot and refuse beyond quota.

title: Accelerator pools are separate from control pools
statement: Persistent/custom accelerator workloads run in GPU pools separated from control pools with taints, priority and quota.
rationale: Accelerator jobs sharing control capacity starve control services.

verification.check: Separate tainted GPU pools planned.

notes: GKE GPU pools conflict with ADR 0024.

title: TPU7x only for workloads with measured framework/topology fit
statement: TPU7x (Ironwood) is used only for training/inference whose JAX/PyTorch and topology benefit is measured, never assumed for all workloads.
rationale: Accelerators chosen by fashion rather than measurement waste budget.

verification.check: The compute router admits a TPU rung only with a recorded benchmark showing benefit.

title: Solver and simulation pools autoscale by queue with Spot
statement: Symbolic solvers, simulations, tournament and evaluation run on CPU pools that autoscale by queue depth and use Spot for disposable simulations.
rationale: Fixed pools are idle or saturated; on-demand capacity for disposable jobs is overspend.

verification.check: A batch/job pool scaled by queue with Spot is planned.

title: Quantum gateway is a budgeted, optional dependency with classical fallback
statement: IBM Quantum access goes through a gateway as a budgeted external dependency with benchmark tracking and a mandatory classical fallback.
rationale: A QPU treated as required makes vendor queue time a decision dependency.

verification.check: Every quantum path computes a classical baseline and a failed classical baseline reports nothing; only the optimisation zone may reach IBM.

title: Cloud Scheduler/Workflows are peripheral ops jobs only
statement: Cloud Scheduler and Workflows run only scheduled governance/maintenance ops jobs and never form the core event backbone.
rationale: A scheduler used as a bus has no ordering, replay or idempotency.

verification.check: No scheduler/workflow resource targets a Fabric or trading endpoint.

title: Pub/Sub is not used for internal messaging
statement: Google Pub/Sub is not used for internal pub/sub, control, outcome or tick journals; the native Rust Fabric defines those semantics.
rationale: A managed bus with its own delivery semantics silently replaces the ones the platform proved.

sources.section: §19.1 Deliberately not used as core internal messaging

verification.check: No Pub/Sub topic beyond the recorded secret-rotation notice and no Pub/Sub client crate; adding a topic fails.

title: Managed Kafka is never the core backbone
statement: Managed Service for Apache Kafka is not the core event backbone; it may exist only as an optional external compatibility bridge when a partner requires Kafka.
rationale: Same failure as Pub/Sub: borrowed semantics nobody proved.

sources.section: §19.1 Deliberately not used as core internal messaging

verification.check: No Kafka resource or client crate; a bridge, if any, is stateless at the edge.

title: Eventarc is peripheral automation only
statement: Eventarc is not part of core internal eventing and is used only for peripheral Google-service automation that never becomes an application dependency.
rationale: Hidden triggers become undocumented application dependencies.

sources.section: §19.1 Deliberately not used as core internal messaging

verification.check: No Terraform or workflow provisions Eventarc.

title: Cloud Tasks is not an internal general queue
statement: Cloud Tasks is not used as an internal general queue; only isolated customer-facing workflows whose semantics specifically fit may use it.
rationale: A task queue as internal bus has no replay or ordering contract.

sources.section: §19.1 Deliberately not used as core internal messaging

verification.check: No Terraform or workflow provisions Cloud Tasks.

title: Venue feed and orders connect directly to the Reflex node
statement: Market data and orders flow directly between the venue (FIX/WS/native TCP/UDP) and the Reflex node synchronously; this is the only true trading path.
rationale: Any intermediary on the venue path adds latency and a failure domain to every order.

verification.check: The node binds the venue feed and gateway itself; no broker, proxy or service sits between. A feed routed through Fabric fails the check.

notes: Real venue order submission is refused by ADR 0003; only the simulated gateway is reachable.

title: Reflex peers coordinate directly over a fast ephemeral link
statement: Reflex nodes exchange cross-region opportunity/reservation coordination directly with peer nodes (direct QUIC), with no durable replay requirement.
rationale: Routing peer coordination through the centre or the Fabric doubles latency on the only cross-region time-critical exchange.

verification.check: Two nodes exchange epoch/reservation frames over a direct socket with no centre hop.

notes: QUIC needs a dependency ADR 0002/0009 do not admit; MESH-038 records it as blocked.

title: Reflex journals to regional Fabric asynchronously over mTLS
statement: The Reflex node journals ticks, decisions, outcomes and control acknowledgments to the regional Fabric asynchronously (QUIC/mTLS); Fabric failure cannot block an order.
rationale: A synchronous journal write turns a broker stall into a trading halt.

verification.check: With the writer stalled, ship returns immediately and the pass proceeds; the node's main wires the writer. Removing the non-blocking ship fails.

notes: mTLS/QUIC needs a dependency or sidecar.

title: Control services publish policy and envelopes through Fabric
statement: Warm control services publish policy, research, capital and risk-envelope events to the regional Fabric asynchronously.
rationale: Point-to-point control delivery has no replay or ordering record.

verification.check: A policy/envelope publish lands on a Fabric P0 stream and a cell consumes it from there.

title: Warm consumers pull ordered partitions and replay
statement: Warm services consume ordered Fabric partitions by pull/stream and can replay from committed offsets.
rationale: Consumers without offsets lose or double-process records after restart.

verification.check: A consumer group resumes from its committed offset after restart.

title: Fabric segments archive immutably to Cloud Storage
statement: Sealed Fabric segments are archived immutably to Cloud Storage via private Google access, off the commit path, as a replay source.
rationale: Without an archive the Fabric's retention bound is the replay horizon.

verification.check: fabricd archives sealed segments to a GCS store; a stalled store does not block produce.

title: Fabric sink writes recent features and replay indexes to Bigtable
statement: A Fabric sink writes recent features, time series and replay indexes to Bigtable asynchronously.
rationale: Feature lookups against the journal are too slow for warm services.

verification.check: Sink consumes a stream and rows appear in Bigtable.

title: Fabric BigQuery sink streams research data and may lag
statement: A Fabric sink streams research/analytics records to BigQuery (Storage Write API) and may lag without trading impact.
rationale: Same as BigQuery row.

verification.check: Sink consumes a stream and rows land; sink lag does not affect producers.

title: Ledger writer commits outcomes idempotently
statement: The ledger writer consumes P1 outcomes and commits them to the authoritative store idempotently, so redelivery and crash never double-book or drop.
rationale: A redelivered fill booked twice, or an offset committed ahead of its postings, corrupts the books silently.

verification.check: For any duplication/redelivery/crash schedule, balances equal a single clean delivery; mutating the dedup rule fails.

title: Training pipelines build datasets from retained stores
statement: Training pipelines build training/evaluation datasets from GCS, BigQuery, Bigtable and Spanner Graph over private Google APIs.
rationale: Datasets assembled ad hoc cannot be reproduced.

verification.check: A dataset manifest names its source snapshots and rebuilds identically.

title: Registry publishes signed package manifests and weights
statement: Training/registry publishes deployment package manifests and weights to Artifact Registry and GCS as signed OCI/model packages.
rationale: Hand-copied model files have no provenance.

verification.check: A promotion produces a signed manifest stored by digest.

title: Package manager verifies signatures before activation
statement: The Reflex package manager stages a model/policy bundle from Artifact Registry/GCS and verifies its signature (KMS) before activation.
rationale: An unverified bundle is arbitrary code on the order path.

verification.check: A bundle with a bad signature is refused before any state changes.

title: Quantum jobs go through controlled egress with no execution dependency
statement: Agent/symbolic workers reach the IBM Quantum gateway only over controlled HTTPS egress, for eligible jobs only, with no execution dependency.
rationale: Uncontrolled egress to a vendor is an exfiltration path and a latency trap.

verification.check: Only the optimisation zone may reach IBM; fastbrain cannot.

title: Environment Git is reconciled by GitOps
statement: Desired state lives in environment Git and is reconciled by Config Sync / Argo CD.
rationale: Imperative deploys drift and cannot be audited.

verification.check: Argo CD applications point at this repo's env directories; dev auto-syncs with prune/self-heal; a manifest outside the gitops tree fails.

notes: Argo CD runs on the ADR 0036 control-plane cluster; Config Sync is not used.

title: Builds push signed, provenance-bearing artifacts
statement: CI pushes artifacts with signatures and provenance (SBOM/attestation) to Artifact Registry.
rationale: An artifact without provenance cannot be traced to a commit.

verification.check: Every pushed digest is attested; the matrix covers every deployable.

title: Telemetry flows through buffering collectors
statement: Telemetry flows via collectors (OTLP) to Cloud Monitoring/Prometheus/Logging/Trace with sampling and buffering protecting production.
rationale: Unbuffered telemetry back-pressures the process emitting it.

verification.check: Collector buffers and drops under pressure without affecting the emitting process.

title: Evidence updates latent state via typed knowledge events
statement: Scout/evidence workers update the NOW Brain's latent state through typed Fabric knowledge events, without storing raw source bytes.
rationale: Raw bytes in the knowledge path carry licensing liability and no structure.

verification.check: Knowledge events are schema-closed and carry no raw payload field.

title: Forecast Router fans multi-horizon questions to the model society
statement: A Forecast Router consumes promoted current-state vectors and surprise events and fans out independent forecasts across microsecond-to-year horizons to specialist models, agents, world models and simulators via Fabric task contracts.
rationale: Single-horizon forecasting misses the horizon where the edge actually is.

verification.check: A router produces per-horizon tasks from a state vector.

title: Model society aggregates forecasts and scores calibration
statement: Model Tournament and Forecast Market aggregate predictions and score calibration against resolved outcomes.
rationale: Unscored forecasts cannot earn or lose influence.

verification.check: Resolved outcomes update a calibration score per forecaster.

title: Conflicting forecasts trigger InformationRequests
statement: When forecasts conflict, the adversarial society issues an InformationRequest to Active Sensing for discriminating evidence where value-of-information is high.
rationale: Disagreement left unresolved is either ignored or acted on blindly.

verification.check: A conflict above threshold produces an InformationRequest with VOI.

title: Meta-Intelligence allocates compute by expected value
statement: Meta-Intelligence issues ComputePlans allocating CPU/GPU/TPU/QPU and agent budgets only where expected uncertainty reduction or economic value justifies the cost.
rationale: Compute spent uniformly is mostly wasted on questions that do not matter.

verification.check: A plan's allocation is justified by an expected-value term and recorded.

title: Compute router dispatches parallel candidates across hardware
statement: The compute router dispatches parallel candidate computations to CPU/GPU/TPU/QPU through native APIs or controlled egress.
rationale: Serial single-backend computation cannot compare methods.

verification.check: One problem fans to multiple backends and results are compared with a classical baseline.

title: Verifier results promote, reweight or retire models
statement: Verifier emits VerificationResults that promote, reweight or retire models and solver policies in the tournament.
rationale: Models that never lose influence accumulate stale authority.

verification.check: A failed verification demotes a model; a passing one may promote.

title: Forecast consensus feeds capital, risk and hedge as distributions
statement: Forecast consensus reaches Capital/Risk/Hedge as ForecastState/WorldBranch contracts carrying full distributions so uncertainty translates into sizing, reserves and hedges.
rationale: Point forecasts discard the tails that sizing must respect.

verification.check: Capital sizing consumes a distribution type including tails.

title: Capital/Risk/Hedge distribute bounded authority to regions
statement: Capital, Risk and Hedge services distribute bounded authority to regions as CapitalGrant, RiskEnvelope and HedgePlan contracts over the Rust Fabric.
rationale: Authority without bounds lets a partitioned region spend beyond plan.

verification.check: A signed bounded grant reaches a cell and the cell refuses beyond it.

title: Cognitive compiler distills signed Reflex packages
statement: The Cognitive Compiler distills validated low-latency capability into signed OCI/model packages for Reflex; live order execution remains local and deterministic.
rationale: Shipping a research model directly to the hot path makes execution non-deterministic.

verification.check: A distilled package is signed and deterministic in replay.

title: Market data is sequence-checked and normalized in memory
statement: Venue market data entering the Reflex adapter is sequence-checked and normalized in memory before any decision.
rationale: A gap applied as if continuous produces a book that never existed.

verification.check: A sequence gap resets/flags the book and replay reproduces the integrity flag.

title: Deterministic local risk gate approves or vetoes every order
statement: Local book/features/reflex model evaluate each event, a deterministic local risk gate approves or vetoes, and only then is the order sent directly to the venue.
rationale: A non-deterministic or remote gate cannot be replayed or relied on during partition.

verification.check: Every refusal is journaled under a gate constant and no order reaches the gateway past a refusal.

notes: Order send to a real venue is paper-only (ADR 0003).

title: Every tick, decision, order and fill reaches Fabric P1/P2
statement: Tick, feature snapshot, decision, order and fill/cancel are appended asynchronously to Fabric P1/P2 topics; a Fabric outage cannot retroactively stall the order.
rationale: Unjournaled decisions cannot be replayed or attributed.

verification.check: Every journal entry reaches P2 and every outcome also reaches P1 with its digest.

title: Replay compares predicted fills and outcomes to actuals
statement: Replay/evaluation compares predicted fills, slippage and outcomes against actual results and emits episodes and model residuals.
rationale: A twin never compared with reality drifts unnoticed.

verification.check: Fill error per venue is recorded on each filled order in LEARN.

title: Candidates are evaluated, signed and promoted through gates
statement: Training uses world and tick history to improve models; candidates are evaluated, signed and promoted through GitOps/model gates.
rationale: An unevaluated candidate on the hot path is an experiment with real consequences.

verification.check: Promotion refuses an unevaluated or digest-changed candidate.

title: Packages activate atomically at an approved epoch with rollback ready
statement: The Reflex package manager stages a new package, activates it atomically at the approved epoch, and keeps the previous package rollback-ready.
rationale: A partially activated package mixes two models in one decision.

verification.check: Activation swaps at the epoch boundary only; rollback restores the parent; a mid-pass swap fails.

title: Observations carry source identity and provenance into immutable evidence
statement: Every scout/crawler/API observation is captured with source identity and provenance and published to regional Fabric plus immutable GCS evidence.
rationale: Evidence without provenance cannot be challenged or trusted.

verification.check: An observation lands with provenance in a retention-locked bucket.

title: Evidence workers normalize entities and corroborate sources
statement: Evidence workers normalize entities, corroborate sources and update trust/confidence; world-model services update the knowledge graph.
rationale: Uncorroborated single-source facts drive decisions.

verification.check: Corroboration changes confidence per source.

title: Ambient models publish research and opportunity tasks
statement: Ambient models detect surprise, novelty or causal implications and publish research/opportunity tasks to Fabric.
rationale: Surprise that creates no task is surprise nobody acts on.

verification.check: A surprise above threshold produces a task.

title: Validated results reach the hot path only as signed packages
statement: A validated research result becomes a strategy/model/risk/capital proposal and reaches execution only through promotion gates as signed policy/model packages, never as an unreviewed direct hot-path call.
rationale: A direct call from research into execution bypasses every review.

verification.check: Cells apply only verified signed payloads; nothing in the edge node depends on cognitive crates.

title: Each cell computes local executable edges from local venue state
statement: Each Reflex cell maintains local venue state and computes its locally executable arbitrage edges.
rationale: Edges computed centrally are stale by the time a cell can act.

verification.check: A cell's desk finds and executes a cycle from its own books.

title: Opportunity/reservation exchange stays off the Fabric
statement: Compressed opportunity/reservation state is exchanged directly over the Reflex Mesh, not through the Fabric.
rationale: Fabric latency and quorum on peer coordination misses the opportunity.

verification.check: No mesh frame type is a Fabric stream.

title: Bounded reservations under opportunity epoch and fencing
statement: Coordinators and participants acquire bounded local reservations using opportunity epoch/fencing and execute legs only under local deterministic risk.
rationale: Two cells reserving against an abandoned cycle double-spend.

verification.check: No leg fires after epoch expiry; FIRE only when every leg is reserved and the loss bound covers recovery.

title: Partial completion follows explicit hedge/unwind rules
statement: Partial completion of a multi-leg cycle follows explicit hedge/unwind saga rules; no path is treated as riskless when atomicity is impossible.
rationale: A stranded leg with no rule becomes an unbounded position.

verification.check: A short leg triggers the declared decomposition/unwind policy and a whole-cycle desk stops on any short leg.

title: All arbitrage intents, fills, hedges and outcomes are journaled and ledgered
statement: All intents, fills, hedges and outcomes of multi-region cycles are journaled to Fabric and ledgered centrally; replay evaluates missed/failed cycles.
rationale: Unledgered hedges are positions the books do not know.

verification.check: A cycle's events appear in P1 and the ledger balances reflect them.

title: Incidents and gaps create scoped engineering goals
statement: An incident, backlog item or Intelligence Expansion gap creates a scoped engineering goal for the autonomous development loop.
rationale: Unscoped agent work sprawls and cannot be reviewed.

verification.check: A goal record is produced from an incident/backlog input.

title: Agent changes are evaluated independently in a sandbox
statement: Planner/coder agents create a branch/PR with tests, and independent test, security and architecture agents evaluate it in a sandbox.
rationale: An agent reviewing its own change is no review.

verification.check: Agent PRs pass the same CI gates and an independent review step.

title: CI runs replay, performance, fuzz, security and IaC gates
statement: CI builds deterministic artifacts and runs Rust replay/performance/fuzz plus security and IaC gates before anything is released.
rationale: A release that skipped a gate is a release nobody verified.

verification.check: Pipeline gates on test, clippy -D warnings, deps, secrets, Terraform; deploy requires tests passed.

title: Release changes only environment Git; Kargo promotes exact digest
statement: The release agent changes only the environment Git repository and Kargo promotes the exact attested digest; rollout mechanics depend on component type.
rationale: Rebuilding per environment ships different bytes than were tested.

verification.check: Stages chain dev→test→stage→prod from one warehouse, never by semver; images pinned by digest.

notes: Blueprint implies a separate environment repo; this platform is one repository.

title: SLO/replay gates trigger rollback on regression
statement: SLO and replay gates observe production; a regression triggers rollback and feeds evidence back to the agent loop.
rationale: A regression nobody gates on persists until a person notices.

verification.check: A degraded release fails the gate and the previous digest is restored.

title: NOW Brain estimates current latent state and uncertainty
statement: Pass-through observations update promoted knowledge and live derived state, and the NOW Brain estimates current latent state and its uncertainty.
rationale: Decisions on a state estimate with no uncertainty over-commit.

verification.check: State estimate carries an uncertainty measure updated per observation.

title: Digital twins propagate candidate worlds into portfolio outcomes
statement: Future-state/digital-twin simulations propagate candidate worlds into prices, liquidity, counterparties and portfolio outcomes.
rationale: Forecasts not propagated to portfolio impact cannot inform sizing.

verification.check: A scenario world produces a portfolio outcome distribution.

title: Capital, risk, confidence and hedge consume full distributions
statement: Capital Society, Risk Brain, Confidence Governor and Hedge Brain consume the full forecast distribution including disagreement and tails and emit bounded CapitalGrant, RiskEnvelope and HedgePlan contracts.
rationale: Ignoring disagreement sizes as if consensus existed.

verification.check: Wider disagreement reduces emitted grant size.

title: Resolved outcomes score forecasts, models, agents, hedges, capital and routing
statement: Resolved outcomes score forecasts, models, agents, hedges, capital decisions and compute-routing choices, closing the self-improvement loop.
rationale: Unscored decisions never improve.

verification.check: LEARN updates scores for each decision class.

title: Fabric loss: reflex continues, spools boundedly, narrows on pressure
statement: If the Fabric is lost, Reflex continues under local policy, buffers bounded critical events to a local spool, and narrows when spool or freshness policy is exceeded.
rationale: Halting on Fabric loss turns a messaging outage into a trading outage; an unbounded spool fills the disk.

verification.check: Spool pressure reads Narrow then Exhausted and the wired cell halts new exposure; ship never blocks.

title: Fabric loss: platform alerts immediately and replays segments
statement: If the Fabric is lost the platform alerts immediately, restores the cluster and replays local spools and GCS segments.
rationale: A silent Fabric outage loses the journal's guarantees unnoticed.

verification.check: An alert fires on broker loss; replay from spool/archive restores continuity.

title: Warm services loss: reflex continues locally without new authority
statement: If regional warm services are lost, Reflex continues local execution with no new warm policy/capital intelligence, Fabric keeps journaling, and other regions may cover eligible functions.
rationale: Cells that stop when the centre stops make the centre a single point of failure.

verification.check: A cut-off cell keeps placing paper orders inside its envelope, shrinks as inputs age and stops at envelope expiry.

title: Ledger loss: trade only within cached envelope until ledger-lag threshold
statement: If Spanner is lost, Reflex continues only within its cached capital/risk envelope until a ledger-lag threshold, with stricter transfer/position actions disabled.
rationale: Trading on capital the ledger has not confirmed overcommits.

verification.check: Orders stop when the envelope expires or the ledger-lag threshold is crossed; transfers are refused while lagging.

title: Ledger loss: outcomes accumulate durably and replay idempotently
statement: If Spanner is lost, outcome partitions accumulate durably in the Fabric and the ledger writer replays idempotently when restored.
rationale: Outcomes dropped during a ledger outage are fills nobody booked.

verification.check: Writer down leaves the checkpoint; on recovery balances equal a clean delivery.

title: Analytics store loss has no hot-path impact
statement: Loss of Bigtable/BigQuery has no direct hot-path impact; research/replay/features degrade while Fabric/GCS preserve source history.
rationale: An analytics dependency on the order path makes warehouse maintenance a trading risk.

verification.check: The edge node's dependency closure contains no Bigtable/BigQuery client.

title: AI platform loss: no new cognition, existing packages continue
statement: If the AI/agent platform is lost, no new cognitive/model output is produced, existing packages continue, and research backlog queues.
rationale: Model-provider outages must not stop execution.

verification.check: Node trades identically with the centre silent.

title: Cross-region loss: local trading continues, peer-dependent cycles disabled
statement: If cross-region networking is lost, local trading continues, multi-region cycles requiring peers are disabled, Fabric mirrors lag and catch up when the link returns, and regional durability stays intact.
rationale: Cycles assuming a missing peer leave one side of a trade with no counterpart.

verification.check: A dark region suspends mirrored legs into it and leaves home-only trading unchanged; an unreadable wire treats all others as dark.

title: Feed loss stops dependent strategies and follows a local playbook
statement: If a venue feed is lost, strategies depending on the stale feed stop, positions are hedged or exited per a local playbook, and incident and reconciliation events are journaled.
rationale: Trading off a frozen book prices orders against a market that moved.

verification.check: A stalled venue feed gets no new order past max_staleness while other venues keep trading; a playbook action is journaled.

title: GitOps loss leaves running system unchanged; break-glass reconciles later
statement: If GitHub/GitOps is lost the running system is unchanged and no new deploys occur; emergency changes use a pre-approved break-glass process later reconciled to Git.
rationale: Control-plane loss deleting workloads turns a tooling outage into a production outage.

verification.check: Cloud Run services carry deletion-policy abandon; a break-glass runbook path exists.

title: Every resource labelled by plane, region, environment, owner and workload
statement: Every project/resource is labelled with plane, region, environment, owner and workload.
rationale: Unlabelled spend cannot be attributed.

verification.check: A scan finds all five labels on every labelable resource.

title: Billing is exported to BigQuery
statement: Billing data is exported to BigQuery.
rationale: Without export, cost cannot be analysed or attributed.

verification.check: A billing export dataset/config exists.

notes: Billing export configuration is billing-account scoped.

title: Cost reported per strategy, model, data source and region
statement: Cost is reported per strategy, model, data source and region where attribution is possible.
rationale: Unattributed cost cannot be weighed against the value it produced.

verification.check: A cost ledger entry carries strategy/model/source/region keys.

title: Hot path is overprovisioned; commitments only after stable sizing
statement: Reflex/Fabric capacity is overprovisioned for latency and failure headroom and is never reactively autoscaled; committed-use/reservations are optimised only after benchmark sizing is stable.
rationale: Autoscaling the hot path adds jitter exactly when load spikes.

verification.check: No autoscaler on execution-node groups.

title: Retention is tiered and derived duplicates are bounded
statement: Tick/journal retention is tiered: hot replay in Fabric/Bigtable, immutable segments in GCS, aggregates in BigQuery; derived duplicates are not retained forever.
rationale: Unbounded duplication is unbounded cost and a second source of truth.

verification.check: Every derived store carries a bounded retention/lifecycle rule.

title: AI work has budgets, quotas and benefit-per-dollar benchmarks
statement: Agents and training families have budget/concurrency quotas, use Spot where safe, and model benefit is benchmarked per dollar and latency.
rationale: Unbudgeted AI spend grows with no measured benefit.

verification.check: An agent exceeding its budget is stopped; cost per benefit is recorded.

title: Autonomous agents have daily/monthly model, build and tool budgets
statement: Autonomous engineering agents get explicit daily/monthly model/build/tool budgets and can be throttled independently of production runtime.
rationale: An agent loop without a budget is an open-ended bill.

verification.check: A spent daily budget refuses further calls and is audited.

title: Cost anomalies raise Fabric/incident tasks
statement: Budgets plus Monitoring/BigQuery anomaly jobs create Fabric/incident tasks.
rationale: An anomaly that only emails someone is found at month end.

verification.check: A billing anomaly fixture produces one journaled task.

title: Cost actions never auto-delete production state
statement: No cost or budget action automatically deletes production state.
rationale: An automated cost cut that deletes a ledger is a catastrophe triggered by a spreadsheet.

verification.check: Budgets carry no programmatic action; adding a Pub/Sub action fails.

title: Six environments: dev, integration, replay, paper, staging, prod
statement: The platform provides dev, integration, replay, paper, staging and prod environments, each with its stated purpose and data/connectivity posture.
rationale: Missing tiers force contract, replay and paper testing into environments not built for them.

verification.check: Each environment has committed tfvars and a project.

title: dev uses mock venues and no production secrets
statement: dev uses synthetic/mock venues, reduced data and no production secrets.
rationale: A dev environment with production secrets is production with weaker controls.

verification.check: dev declares the simulated venue adapter and shares no project with any other environment.

title: integration runs the full Fabric topology at small scale
statement: The integration environment runs the full Rust Fabric topology at small scale with deterministic integration feeds for cross-service contract/schema validation.
rationale: Contracts first meet each other in production otherwise.

verification.check: An integration environment deploys fabricd and consumers.

title: replay environment is read-only with no order routes
statement: The replay environment replays historical tick/world data from read-only curated production-derived data with governance and has no live order routes.
rationale: Replay against writable production data corrupts the record it replays.

verification.check: A replay environment with read-only data grants and no venue route.

title: paper environment: live market data, simulated orders, isolated ledger
statement: The paper environment consumes live market data, routes orders only to a simulator, and keeps its ledger isolated from real capital.
rationale: Paper results on synthetic data overstate a strategy; a ledger shared with capital mixes fiction with money.

verification.check: Feed is a real venue feed; gateway is simulated; ledger parks any fill not marked simulated.

title: staging validates scale, failure and game days with separate credentials
statement: Staging provides production-like scale and failure/game-day validation with separate accounts/credentials, canary packages and no uncontrolled live capital.
rationale: Failure modes first seen in production.

verification.check: Stage project has its own identities and canary promotion.

title: prod: live bounded execution with strict isolation and signed artifacts
statement: prod runs live bounded execution with strict region/project isolation, reserved capacity and signed artifacts only.
rationale: Unsigned or shared-project production is unauditable.

verification.check: Prod admits only attested digests in an isolated project with reservations.

notes: Live execution conflicts with ADR 0003 (paper trading only).

title: Promote the same digest; environment differences come from signed config
statement: Every environment receives the same digest and schema/model version; environment-specific behaviour comes from signed configuration and authorized secrets, never from rebuilding code.
rationale: Rebuilt-per-environment code is untested code.

verification.check: One warehouse digest flows through stages; config differs only by signed inputs.

title: Quarterly regional-loss game day
statement: A quarterly game day removes one execution region from service/control networking and verifies other regions continue, mirrors/recovery behave, and no cross-region arbitrage assumes the missing peer.
rationale: Region-loss behaviour never exercised is region-loss behaviour unknown.

verification.check: A scheduled run record with observed outcomes exists each quarter.

title: Monthly zonal failure game day
statement: A monthly game day terminates the Reflex primary or Fabric zone replicas and proves fencing, quorum, failover and bounded outcome loss.
rationale: Untested failover fails the first time it is needed.

verification.check: Monthly drill record with measured outcome loss.

title: Broker backpressure drill: priority QoS and bounded memory
statement: A drill freezes a sink and fills consumer lag, verifying priority QoS and no broker memory explosion.
rationale: A slow consumer that grows broker memory takes the broker down for everyone.

verification.check: Broker memory stays bounded and P0/P1 keep priority under a frozen sink.

title: Ledger outage drill: P1 retention, capital freshness, idempotent catch-up
statement: A drill denies ledger writes and verifies Fabric P1 retention, local capital freshness degradation, then idempotent catch-up.
rationale: Idempotency proven only in unit tests may not survive a real outage.

verification.check: Drill record shows no lost or doubled outcomes.

title: Bad model drill: degraded candidate blocked or rolled back
statement: A drill promotes an intentionally degraded candidate in nonprod/staging and verifies the shadow/replay/SLO gate blocks or rolls it back.
rationale: A gate never shown to fire is a gate that may not.

verification.check: Degraded candidate refused or rolled back.

title: Bad schema is rejected before consumers break
statement: An incompatible Fabric schema is rejected by CI and by the runtime registry before any production consumer breaks.
rationale: A breaking schema change found by a consumer is found after data is lost.

verification.check: Registering a breaking change without a version bump is refused; produce under an unregistered schema is refused; a CI schema lock fails on drift.

title: Agent compromise simulation proves boundaries hold
statement: A drill gives an autonomous dev agent malicious instruction/input and verifies secret, network, merge and prod-deploy boundaries prevent authority escalation.
rationale: Agent boundaries never attacked are assumed, not known.

verification.check: Drill record shows each boundary refused.

title: Periodic rebuild from zero proves no console dependency
statement: Periodically rebuild a regional cluster and a nonprod Fabric cluster from Terraform/Git/artifacts, proving no undocumented console dependency.
rationale: Hidden console state makes disaster recovery impossible.

verification.check: A scheduled up/down run from empty succeeds.

title: Build phase 0: Foundations
statement: Phase 0 (Foundations) delivers: org/folders/projects, IAM/PAM, Terraform modules, NCC/VPC/DNS/firewalls, KMS/CA, audit/SCC, GitHub WIF, meeting its exit test before later phases depend on it.
rationale: Later phases built on an unproven foundation inherit its defects.

verification.check: Each listed deliverable exists and its exit test passes.

title: Build phase 1: Supply chain
statement: Phase 1 (Supply chain) delivers: Cloud Build private pools, Artifact Registry, provenance/SBOM, Binary Authorization, GitOps management cluster, Config Sync/Argo/Kargo/Rollouts, meeting its exit test before later phases depend on it.
rationale: Later phases built on an unproven foundation inherit its defects.

verification.check: Each listed deliverable exists and its exit test passes.

title: Build phase 2: Rust Fabric MVP
statement: Phase 2 (Rust Fabric MVP) delivers: single region 3 brokers, schemas/client, RF3 journal, consumer offsets, GCS archive, OTel; chaos tests before application adoption, meeting its exit test before later phases depend on it.
rationale: Later phases built on an unproven foundation inherit its defects.

verification.check: Each listed deliverable exists and its exit test passes.

title: Build phase 3: One Reflex Cell
statement: Phase 3 (One Reflex Cell) delivers: one venue/asset shard, local risk/order flow, async Fabric journal, replay and paper trading, meeting its exit test before later phases depend on it.
rationale: Later phases built on an unproven foundation inherit its defects.

verification.check: Each listed deliverable exists and its exit test passes.

title: Build phase 4: Financial truth
statement: Phase 4 (Financial truth) delivers: Spanner ledger writer/idempotency, reconciliation, capital/risk envelope contracts, meeting its exit test before later phases depend on it.
rationale: Later phases built on an unproven foundation inherit its defects.

verification.check: Each listed deliverable exists and its exit test passes.

title: Build phase 5: Data plane
statement: Phase 5 (Data plane) delivers: GCS retained tick/internal archive and compact knowledge packs, Bigtable, BigQuery, Knowledge Catalog, replay/feature sinks, data contracts, meeting its exit test before later phases depend on it.
rationale: Later phases built on an unproven foundation inherit its defects.

verification.check: Each listed deliverable exists and its exit test passes.

title: Build phase 6: Regional service plane
statement: Phase 6 (Regional service plane) delivers: GKE asset/capital/risk/evidence/API services, Fabric consumer scaling, Redis cache, meeting its exit test before later phases depend on it.
rationale: Later phases built on an unproven foundation inherit its defects.

verification.check: Each listed deliverable exists and its exit test passes.

notes: GKE conflicts with ADR 0024; Cloud Run satisfies the plane under that decision.

title: Build phase 7: Multi-region
